name: Diligence Question Builder

inputs.name: Thesis pillars and key risks (or the teaser/CIM)
Process stage and access level (management meeting, data room, expert calls)

steps.title: Map thesis to evidence
steps.detail: For each pillar: what would have to be true, and what data proves it?

steps.title: Map risks to tests
steps.detail: For each risk: what’s the cheapest fastest way to size it?

steps.title: Rank by kill-power
steps.detail: Questions that could kill the deal go first — you want bad news early and cheap.

steps.title: Route by source
steps.detail: Management vs data room vs experts vs desktop. Don’t burn a management meeting on data-room questions.

steps.title: Draft the asks
steps.detail: Specific, answerable questions — "walk me through churn by cohort for FY24-26", not "tell us about retention".

steps.title: Delegate 1
steps.detail: Generating candidate questions per workstream from the thesis

steps.title: Delegate 2
steps.detail: Grouping and deduplicating into a tracker format

steps.title: Delegate 3
steps.detail: Drafting data-request lists in standard form

sections.name: Prioritised diligence question list by workstream
sections.detail: Generate and rank diligence questions from the investment thesis: for each pillar and each key risk, what evidence would confirm or kill it, who has that evidence, and what to ask first when management time is scarce.

outputs.sourcePolicy: Every figure cites the page or filing it was read from; nothing is stated without a source.

verification.description: Questions are answerable from the named source
No question already answered in materials you hold — that costs credibility
Every thesis pillar has at least one confirming and one killing test
Top-5 list fits a 45-minute management meeting
Each question names its source and owner

humanCheckpoints: Which three questions matter most — the kill-power ranking
What you’re willing to take on trust vs must verify
When you have enough to advance vs walk

display.jobToBeDone: Build a prioritised diligence list that attacks the thesis, not a generic checklist.
